clue.text: Almost within range?

definitions.meaning: close enough to reach or hit, as a target in range

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are an idiom: approximately, and literally close by within reach.

clue.text: It's always right to follow the first mate

indicators.note: the letter for right comes after the first mate, following her in the answer

parts.note: Eve was Adam's partner, the first wife in Genesis

explanation.surface: A ship's officer defers to the first mate as a matter of course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First mate' suggests a ship, but it is Eve, the first wife; 'to follow' puts R after her.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: forever, at all times.

clue.text: Was abusive, yet guarded?

definitions.meaning: fenced in with rails, as a protective barrier

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: scolded angrily, and enclosed by protective fencing bars.

clue.text: Irritates by the unnecessary loss of a point

indicators.note: loss tells us the compass letter drops out of the longer word

parts.note: S is south, a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Someone is annoyed when a game point is thrown away for nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to goad or provoke someone persistently.

clue.text: Takes advantage and gains three points on centre court

indicators.note: centre picks out the middle letter of the word court

parts.note: S, E and S are three compass points: south, east, south

explanation.surface: A tennis player exploits an opening and wins three quick points on Centre Court.
explanation.walkthrough: Centre Court is Wimbledon's main tennis court; here 'centre' takes U from COURT, and 'three points' are compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: exploits, employs for one's own benefit.

clue.text: At heart he'd a desire to get married

indicators.note: at heart says the craving sits in the middle of the words he'd

parts.note: an itch is a restless craving

explanation.surface: A man confesses he longed deep down to settle down and wed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At heart' looks like 'deep down' in the surface, but it is the container signal; 'to get' is only a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: getting hitched is informal slang for being wed.

clue.text: From vice I'd reformed in stir, possibly? On the contrary

definitions.text: From vice I'd reformed in stir, possibly? On the contrary

indicators.note: reformed means the letters are shaped anew into another word

explanation.surface: A prisoner claims to have turned from crime while inside, but the opposite is true.
explanation.walkthrough: Stir is slang for prison. 'On the contrary' turns the boast round: the answer is someone who did not reform in jail and offends again.
explanation.definitionFit: A habitual reoffender is the opposite of a convict who mended their ways in prison.

clue.text: Meals and beers set out for get together again

indicators.note: set out means the letters are laid out in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Food and drink are laid out for a reunion party.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to gather once more after parting.

clue.text: You might say it when offering a gift-or present

definitions.text: You might say it when offering a gift
definitions.meaning: the word said while holding something out: take this

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: an exclamation when handing something over, and being in attendance.

clue.text: An improvement in culture

definitions.meaning: a small change that makes something better

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: an enhancement, and cultivated sophistication of manners.

clue.text: Publications for entertainers?

definitions.meaning: stand-up comedians who make people laugh

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: cartoon magazines, and funny performers on stage.

clue.text: On board get rotten seats

indicators.note: on board is the convention for going inside the steamship letters

parts.note: SS stands for steamship, the vessel one goes on board

explanation.surface: Aboard a neglected vessel, the seating is decaying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On board' is a crossword convention: going on board a steamship puts a word between its two letters. 'get rotten' is said of eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a rider's seat on a horse or bicycle.

clue.text: It's wet and fine at the same time

definitions.text: It's wet and fine at the same time

parts.words: It's wet and fine at the same time
parts.note: fine here means made of tiny droplets, not sunny: a misty drizzle that soaks while seeming harmless

explanation.definitionFit: A Highland weather term for thick drizzling fog, very fine droplets that still soak you.

clue.text: She serves school

parts.note: serves reads as working for a school, but means serving lunches to pupils

explanation.definitionFit: A woman employed to dish out midday meals to children in a canteen.

clue.text: Go into liquidation when working hard?

definitions.text: Go into liquidation when working hard?

parts.words: Go into liquidation when working hard?
parts.note: liquidation suggests bankruptcy, but means turning to liquid: the body perspires under exertion

explanation.definitionFit: To perspire, giving off moisture through the skin during exertion.

clue.text: Refuse to go through all the cases?

definitions.meaning: in grammar, recite a noun's forms in every case, as Latin pupils do

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: reject an offer, and list the case endings of a noun.

clue.text: New or old slaver

indicators.note: new suggests the letters are made over into a fresh form

explanation.surface: A slave trader, whether new or old in the business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slaver' looks like a slave trader, but it is the verb: to dribble.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to let saliva run from the mouth.

clue.text: Pulls back the grass

indicators.note: back tells us the synonym for pulls is read in reverse

explanation.surface: Someone yanks up turf from the lawn.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an expanse of short turf or lawn.

clue.text: Has a tumble in snow

indicators.note: a tumble tosses the letters of the following word about

explanation.surface: Someone takes a fall in the snowdrifts.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: possesses, holds as property.

clue.text: Branch member

definitions.meaning: a large bough of a tree
an arm or leg of the body

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a tree bough, and an arm or leg.

clue.text: Great figure, a master to his mate

parts.note: MA is a Master of Arts
Gog is the giant always paired with the one the answer names

explanation.surface: An imposing person is a master-figure to a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: Gog and Magog are giant figures in London legend, statues of them stand in the Guildhall.
explanation.definitionFit: Legend: a huge giant effigy, one of a famous pair of guardian giants.

clue.text: Servants turn in between lunch and dinner?

indicators.note: between places the flipped word inside the meals
turn says the word in is flipped round

explanation.surface: Domestic staff take a break in the afternoon lull between meals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn in' looks like going to bed; 'turn' gives the reversal and 'between' the container. The question mark flags lunch and dinner as examples.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: lowly domestic workers doing humble tasks.

clue.text: Coward and criminal come up in a ship

indicators.note: come up in a down clue means the pieces are read upwards, backwards

parts.note: lag is slang for a convict, an old lag

explanation.surface: A cowardly man and a crook surface aboard a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coward' looks like a timid person, but it is the playwright Noel Coward; 'come up' reverses NOEL + LAG.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a large Spanish sailing vessel of the Armada era.

clue.text: Salad greenery and French dressing in a light basket

explanation.surface: A salad of leaves with French vinaigrette served in a little basket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French dressing' looks like vinaigrette, but 'and French' gives ET.
explanation.definitionFit: A metal cage on a pole holding burning fuel as a torch or beacon.

clue.text: Infantile habits

parts.note: habits means clothing, as a monk's habit, so this is a baby's outfit, not childish behaviour

explanation.definitionFit: A complete set of clothes and linen prepared for a newborn baby.

clue.text: Expect brawl in bar

indicators.note: a brawl is a scuffle that throws the letters into disorder

explanation.surface: A pub-goer anticipates a fight breaking out in the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' looks like a pub but is the preposition meaning 'but'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: apart from, excluding, as in all bar one.

clue.text: One must back the law to some degree in this African state

indicators.note: back here means go behind, so the numeral comes after the legal word

parts.note: MA is a Master of Arts degree
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Each citizen must support the rule of law to a degree in this country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' looks like support, but it means stand behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a landlocked country in south-east Africa.

clue.text: He's American at heart

indicators.note: at heart takes the central letters of the word American

explanation.surface: A man is a true American deep down.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a man's first name, so a he.

clue.text: It's hotly tipped so raise the stake

indicators.note: raise in a down clue sends the stake word upward, read in reverse

parts.note: an ante is a poker stake

explanation.surface: A gambler with a hot tip ups the bet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hotly tipped' sounds like a racing favourite, but means a mountain with a fiery peak.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a Sicilian volcano, whose summit spews hot lava.

clue.text: Mere agents might make them

indicators.note: might make says the letters can be fashioned into a new word

explanation.walkthrough: Mere negotiators can make deals, and the letters of the two words also make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Deals or contracts that negotiators broker between parties.

clue.text: Such pomposity is not a front

definitions.meaning: airs and pretension, putting on a superior manner
a flank, as opposed to the front of something

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: arrogant swagger, and a flank rather than the face.

clue.text: In which the reserves run out

definitions.text: In which the reserves run out

parts.words: In which the reserves run out
parts.note: run out suggests supplies being exhausted, but means substitute players taking the field

explanation.definitionFit: A club's reserve squad, made of players not picked for the first selection.
